correctedCritiques.con-atheism-nonbelief-burden: Strongest feature: The reply differentiates general nonbelief from universal divine nonexistence, then uses an observational illustration to explain why deity descriptions can warrant positive rejection when their consequences conflict with reality. Principal limitation: That burden clarification does not eliminate the logical, metaphysical, or justificatory commitments, so it partially answers the affirmative's wider transcendental challenge. Live burden: The negative must preserve this distinction while acknowledging those commitments, whereas the affirmative must demonstrate that examining them establishes Orthodox necessity rather than confirming that every reasoner has commitments. Locked score: The very strong band reflects precise qualification, direct responsiveness, illustration, and evidential scope, with reservation because propositional nonbelief receives fuller treatment than the foundations underlying skeptical reasoning practices.
correctedCritiques.pro-skeptical-neutrality-commitments: Strongest feature: The reply grants neutrality about the God proposition while observing that suspended judgment still employs logical rules, metaphysical assumptions, and justificatory standards open to evaluation. Principal limitation: Identifying commitments neither transfers the affirmative burden nor establishes that skeptical nonbelief conceals an atheistic worldview, and their existence provides no inference to an Orthodox foundation. Live burden: The affirmative must identify contradictions within the skeptic's commitments and connect their resolution to Orthodox theology, while respecting the distinction between neutrality about God and neutrality about reasoning. Locked score: The very strong band reflects careful qualification, direct engagement, force, and correction of a broad neutrality claim, moderated because it opens evaluation without completing the theological argument required.
